honest_framing.m2_engagement_in_principle: YES — placing nonzero phase on the flipped edge's SOURCE node (phi_L=0.9) plus complex hopping exp(i*d_phi) drops corr(M1,M2) from 1.0 to 0.0: the orientation-flip CAN be observable.
honest_framing.m2_why_notebook_passes_its_inert: Notebook keeps the flipped edge's source at phi=0 in both M2 (edge L->M, phi_L=0) and M3 (edge 2->0, phi_2=0); d_phi(flip)=d_phi(nonflip) identically, so the T-flip is inert in all three sweeps. The PASSes rest on an operator that never engages.
honest_framing.m2_numerical_degeneracy: This lift is numerically degenerate (direct S->M path saturates M's magnitude; both M1/M2 flat ~14) — it demonstrates engagement is POSSIBLE but does not cleanly exhibit a gated profile. A cleaner interferometer (balanced 2-path amplitudes, no dominant direct edge) is needed for a gated-profile demonstration.
honest_framing.m3_4pi_status: No. On this complex-hopping lift the closed loop with one T-flip shows NO spinor sign flip (psi(phi+2pi)+psi(phi) ~ 2*psi, i.e. 2pi-periodic). A true 4pi double-cover requires the anti-unitary time-reversal T: psi -> conj(psi) on the flipped arm (Kramers pairing), which this phase-sign-flip model is not.
honest_framing.bottom_line: Theory is not refuted; the notebook's implementation is. The T-flip and 4pi claims are UNVERIFIED because the sweeps never engage the orientation operator and the M3 test is amplitude-only. Wall stays gated.
